We also discuss cryogenic fuel markets— particularly future projections of production and/or demand and fuel prices—and infrastructure operations at airports using LH , LNG, and LE on board aircraft. 2 Cryogenic fuel is an energy source that must be stored, transported, and handled at extremely low temperatures—typically below −150°C—to remain in a liquid phase at or near atmospheric pressure. Liquefaction is required to generate a cryogenic fuel because the fuel would otherwise exist in gaseous form with lower volumetric energy density. Even though LE has a boiling point above −150°C, we include it as a cryogenic fuel in this report because it still requires liquefaction and insulated storage tanks similar to LNG and LH . 2 Generally, there is more information available for hydrogen due to extensive research for its use as a transportation fuel in both on-road and off-road applications, including aviation. LNG is primarily used for exporting natural gas, with limited use as an on-road fuel for heavy-duty trucking and a small but growing market as a marine fuel. Ethane is primarily used for ethylene production, with limited research for use in transportation applications. 4.1 Cryogenic Fuel Production Technologies and General Distribution Methods This subsection covers the production of LH , LNG, and LE, as well as general transportation 2 approaches. In the United States, about 10 MMT of hydrogen is produced per year, with most being consumed for petroleum refining, ammonia production, and other chemical production (DOE 2023a). In comparison, global hydrogen production is estimated around 100 MMT/yr in 2023, with China as the largest producer and with the same industrial consumption markets as the United States (IEA 2024a). In net-zero scenarios, potential hydrogen production and consumption could reach more than 400 MMT/yr globally for all end uses (IEA 2023).
